# AN/PRC-117G Radio
The AN/PRC-117G is the RTO manpack radio.
Wear it on your back, load the nets you need, and use [color=#3FCF8E]:r[/color] to transmit through the active slot. A powered radio also works as a relay for nearby friendly headsets.
Only trained roles can open the radio panel and transmit through it.
GOVFOR trained roles: - Radio Telephone Operator - Commander - Officer Adjutant - Advisor
CLF trained roles: - Cell Leader
Nearby soldiers do not need training to use the relay. They only need to be near a worn, powered radio carrying their net.
## Quick Setup
Do this before stepping off.
- Wear the radio in your [bold]back slot[/bold]. - Alt-click the radio or use the verb menu. - Select [bold]Open Radio Panel[/bold]. - Press [bold]+ ADD NET[/bold]. - Give the slot a short label, such as [color=#3FCF8E]CMD[/color]. - Press [bold]TUNE[/bold]. - Pick a named net from the [bold]NET[/bold] tab. - Click the slot row so it highlights. - Insert COMSEC fill if needed. - Set a callsign if you want one.
Transmit with:
[color=#3FCF8E]:r Message here.[/color]
## Slots
The radio can hold [bold]four[/bold] slots.
Use them for command, squad, JTAC, MP, or any other net you expect to need. The slot label is only for you. It does not change the net.
[bold]Button[/bold]
[bold]Use[/bold]
[bold]Note[/bold]
[bold]NET[/bold]
Pick a named faction net.
Normal setup method.
[bold]FREQ[/bold]
Enter a raw frequency.
Used for direct frequencies or enemy nets.
[bold]CLEAR[/bold]
Clear the slot.
Keeps the label.
[bold]DEL[/bold]
Delete the slot.
The next slot is selected if needed.
Click a slot row to make it active. [color=#3FCF8E]:r[/color] always uses the active slot.
Frequencies may be typed with or without a dot.
[color=#3FCF8E]1606[/color] and [color=#3FCF8E]1.606[/color] are the same frequency.
## Callsigns
A callsign is added before every radio message you send.
Type it into [bold]CALLSIGN[/bold] and press [bold]SET[/bold]. Callsigns can be up to 12 characters and are converted to uppercase.
Example:
Callsign set: [bold]LIMA-6[/bold]
You type: [color=#3FCF8E]:r All elements, advance.[/color]
Others hear: [bold]LIMA-6 All elements, advance.[/bold]
Clear the callsign field and press [bold]SET[/bold] to remove it.
## Direct Frequencies
A slot with a frequency but no named net becomes a direct frequency.
Anyone with a [textlink="headset" link="AU14CommsHeadsets"] tuned to the same frequency can talk on it.
Without a relay: - Clean inside [bold]30 tiles[/bold]. - Light garble up to [bold]50 tiles[/bold]. - No signal past [bold]50 tiles[/bold].
With a powered AN/PRC carrying that frequency: - The radio bridges the signal. - Both users must be within [bold]50 tiles[/bold] of the radio.
Use [color=#3FCF8E]:r[/color] when the radio slot is active.
Use [color=#3FCF8E]:x[/color] from a tuned headset.
## Operating Modes
Press [bold]MODE[/bold] to cycle mode.
[bold]Mode[/bold]
[bold]Use[/bold]
[bold]Good[/bold]
[bold]Bad[/bold]
[bold]FH[/bold]
Combat radio work under enemy EW.
Jamming is reduced by one tier.
Uses 1.5x battery. Small DF signature.
[bold]SC[/bold]
Normal radio work when jamming is not active.
Efficient. No DF signature if secured.
No jamming resistance.
[bold]CT[/bold]
Secure AN/PRC to AN/PRC traffic.
No readable enemy intercept. No DF signature.
Needs fill. Normal headsets cannot read it.
[bold]PT[/bold]
Open broadcast or dying battery.
Uses 0.5x battery.
Anyone can read it. Worst DF risk.
Rule of thumb: - [bold]FH[/bold] if enemy jamming is active. - [bold]SC[/bold] for normal secured traffic. - [bold]CT[/bold] for command traffic between AN/PRCs. - [bold]PT[/bold] only when open traffic is acceptable.
## Jamming
FH reduces jamming by one tier.
- Heavy becomes medium. - Medium becomes light. - Light is ignored.
Unlike a normal headset, the AN/PRC can still transmit from inside a jammer field. The message may degrade, but it is not blocked outright.
## MON, SCAN, and SQL
[bold]MON[/bold] is receive-only mode. You hear all loaded nets, but [color=#3FCF8E]:r[/color] is blocked until MON is turned off. Headset keys still work.
[bold]SCAN[/bold] listens to all loaded nets. When traffic comes in, the radio switches the active slot to that net. It does not switch back by itself.
[bold]SQL[/bold] controls squelch. It filters noise, not clean traffic.
[bold]SQL[/bold]
[bold]Effect[/bold]
[bold]0[/bold]
Everything passes, including heavy static.
[bold]1[/bold]
Blocks heavy static.
[bold]2[/bold]
Blocks medium jammer garble.
[bold]3[/bold]
Default. Blocks normal jammer garble.
[bold]4[/bold]
Maximum filtering. May cut weak relay signals.
If you are near a jammer and only hear clicks, lower SQL to 2 or 1.
## COMSEC Fill
COMSEC fill is a physical card.
Insert the card into the radio. The COMSEC panel will show [bold]SECURED[/bold].
Only one fill card can be loaded at a time.
The slot accepts any faction card. A captured enemy card can be used to read their secured traffic.
Faction headsets already carry their own net keys. The AN/PRC needs fill to join that protection. If you transmit on a faction net without fill, the radio warns you. The message still sends, but it goes out in the clear.
An unfilled RTO can expose an otherwise secure net.
## If Capture Is Likely
Do not let a live fill card get taken.
- [bold]ZEROIZE[/bold] ejects the card into your hand. If your hands are full, it drops at your feet. - [bold]DESTROY[/bold] deletes the card.
If a fill card is captured, order [bold]RECRYPTO[/bold] with a current card loaded.
Recrypto makes older cards stale. That includes the captured one.
Fresh cards still need to be ordered through normal supply.
A stale card is marked [bold]STALE[/bold] when examined or shown in the panel.
## Transmit Power
Press [bold]TX[/bold] to change transmit power.
[bold]Power[/bold]
[bold]Range[/bold]
[bold]Battery[/bold]
[bold]DF Signature[/bold]
[bold]LO[/bold]
60 percent relay range.
Half cost.
Half signature.
[bold]MED[/bold]
Standard range.
Standard cost.
Standard signature.
[bold]HI[/bold]
About 150 percent range.
Double cost.
Double signature.
Use LO when your people are close.
Use MED by default.
Use HI to reach distant elements. Send the message, then move.
## Direction Finding
Enemy EW can locate radio transmissions with a DF signature.
Higher risk: - PT mode. - Faction net without matching fill. - FH mode, even when secured. - HI power. - Repeated transmissions from the same place. - Transmitting near enemy jamming.
Secured SC and CT have no DF signature.
If you must transmit with a signature, keep it short and move before sending again.
## Radio Check
Press [bold]RADIO CHECK[/bold] to check coverage on the active net.
The radio sends:
[bold]RADIO CHECK, HOW COPY, OVER[/bold]
You get a private report showing which stations are in clear or degraded range.
Use it before moving out, after repositioning, or after setting up retrans.
If you run the check inside enemy jamming, it also gives a bearing to the strongest jammer.
## Retrans Stations
The AN/PRC does not have to be worn to relay.
Drop it and use [bold]Set Up Retrans[/bold] to plant it as a retrans station. RTO training is required.
A retrans station: - Relays its loaded faction nets. - Keeps logging traffic. - Drains battery. - Keeps its presets and fill card.
Protect retrans sites. Anyone can use [bold]Pack Up Radio[/bold], including the enemy.
If the line moves, pack it up, zeroize it, or destroy the fill.
## Power and Antenna
The radio uses a battery in its own slot.
It drains slowly while idle and faster when transmitting or running radio checks.
Carry spare batteries if you expect heavy traffic.
The radio starts with a [bold]whip[/bold] antenna. It works while moving.
A [bold]mast[/bold] antenna gives better range while stationary. If you move with it, range drops below the whip.
Use mast antennas at command posts or retrans sites.
## Intercepting Enemy Traffic
Tune a slot to an enemy frequency with [bold]FREQ[/bold].
If their signal reaches you, intercepted traffic appears in [color=#FF6B6B]red text[/color] and is recorded in the net log.
What you hear depends on their COMSEC.
[bold]Enemy Traffic[/bold]
[bold]What You Get[/bold]
Headset traffic
Static without their fill.
Secured AN/PRC
Static without their fill.
Unfilled AN/PRC
Readable.
PT traffic
Readable.
FH traffic
Readable if in the clear. Light interference unless you have their fill.
CT traffic
Invisible without their fill.
A current enemy fill card lets you read their secured traffic until they order recrypto.
Your radio only relays your own faction nets. Tuning an enemy frequency lets you listen. It does not extend their net.
## Net Log
The net log stores the last [bold]50[/bold] entries while the radio is powered.
It records: - Your [color=#3FCF8E]:r[/color] transmissions. - Your headset transmissions. - Incoming traffic on the active net. - Incoming traffic on all loaded nets if MON or SCAN is enabled.
Use it to check missed traffic or confirm that an order was sent.
## Status Display
The top of the panel shows radio status.
- [bold]PWR[/bold] shows power. - [bold]LINK[/bold] shows link state. - [bold]MODE[/bold] shows the current mode. - [bold]BIT[/bold] shows built-in test status. - [bold]FAULT[/bold] shows problems.
[bold]READY[/bold] means the radio is worn and has an active net.
[bold]NO NET[/bold], [bold]STBY[/bold], or [bold]NOT WORN[/bold] means you need to check setup.
